The department boasts a team of highly qualified faculty members, with many holding Ph.D. degrees from reputed national and international institutes, ensuring a robust academic and research ecosystem for students.

Programs Offered -

The Department offers a comprehensive suite of programs tailored to meet the diverse needs of students and industry:



  • B. Tech in Mechanical Engineering: A mainstream undergraduate program focusing on the core principles of mechanical engineering and their practical applications.

  • M.Tech in Design Engineering: A postgraduate program emphasizing advanced design methodologies, simulation, and innovation in engineering.

  • PhD: Full time and Part time, in the field of Mechanical Engineering
In addition to these mainstream programs, the department also conducts several specialized weekend programs to cater to working professionals and industry needs. These include:

  • B. Tech Mechanical Engineering (Lateral Entry): Designed for BOSCH Ltd. employees.

  • B. Voc in Tool Engineering: Conducted in collaboration with NTTF.

  • Pharmaceutical Manufacturing Technology: Offered in association with Strides Pharma.

  • Industrial Automation: Conducted in partnership with BOSCH Ltd.

  • M.Tech by Research: Focused on professionals from BOSCH Ltd.

Corporate Training -

The Department plays a vital role in upskilling industry professionals through corporate training programs. These initiatives include tailored training sessions for employees of Strides Pharma and Buhler India, ensuring they remain adept at handling emerging challenges in their respective fields.

Innovation Labs -

To nurture future-ready skills, the Department of Mechanical Engineering hosts cutting-edge innovation labs:



  • Industrial Automation Lab: Powered by BOSCH Rexroth, focusing on advanced automation systems and robotics.

  • CAD Modelling Lab: Equipped with tools from Autodesk, this lab provides hands-on experience in 3D modelling and simulation.


These labs empower students to bridge the gap between theoretical knowledge and practical applications, preparing them for the demands of modern industry.

Research and Funding -

The Department has a strong research culture, with faculty members executing numerous funded projects from prestigious organizations such as ARDB, DST-SERB, and CSR funding from Dassault Systems. Major research areas include: Advanced materials and material processing *Renewable energy systems *Sustainable manufacturing practices. Additionally, CSR funding from BETA Simulation Systems has enabled skill development programs, which are followed by job opportunities with major automotive OEMs, ensuring a seamless transition from education to employment.

Excellent Placement Record -

The Department’s focus on holistic student development has resulted in excellent placement outcomes. Students have secured positions in leading multinational corporations and nationally reputed companies. The highest package offered was INR 27 LPA, followed by another impressive offer of INR 17 LPA. Furthermore, students actively participate in various national-level competitions and have consistently won awards, showcasing their skills and innovative potential.

userdata.description:
Anatomy is the scientific study of the human body in detail. It entails gross features, microscopic structure, and development of individual components, basic genetics and clinical aspects. At CDSIMER, The department of anatomy with dedicated full-fledged staff make sure to highlight the exact same under the guidance of Dr Martin Lucas A, Head of the Department who through his passion for the subject has shown keen interest in establishing the department in high standards. The department of anatomy has a best in class, state of the art museum, Dissection hall, Research lab, Histology lab and well equipped demonstration rooms.

The Department of Anatomy museum has a wide collection of dissected specimens with fine details according to various systems of the body, mounted and maintained in specialized jars which facilitate clear and accurate visibility. It also proudly presents Plastinated specimens aimed to last for eternity which the students can touch the organs can touch the organs, in addition two dimensional and three dimensional teaching models authored and innovated by the head of the department which facilitate better understanding of the subject to our dear students.

The dissection hall is well illuminated with natural light with well ventilation. Sufficient cadavers are maintained efficiently with the best storage facility for our student’s academic learning. It also contains standardized equipment’s for the dissection and specimen preparation and sectioning the various structures of the human body.

The Research lab in the department of Anatomy focuses on biomedical research, mainly histological and plastination techniques extending its wings into molecular biology, animal models and stem cell biology.

The histology lab is equipped with the latest microscopes and high resolution audio-visual aids.

The Department of Anatomy also accommodate multiple demonstration rooms with up to date, audio visual aids to encourage and contribute to the students’ academic education. Charts with extremely good surface detailing related to gross anatomy, histology, embryology, comparative anatomy and radiology which is highly used for medical education are displayed throughout the museum, dissection hall and histology lab.

The Department of Anatomy has proven to be a strong asset to CDSIMER and associated institutions and a pivotal for the Medical education of all our students.

Forensic Medicine and Toxicology is broadly classified into Forensic Pathology, Clinical Forensic Medicine and study of poisons and treatment. Forensic Medicine is application of medical knowledge to aid in administration of justice. Further it is classified into Forensic Pathology that deals with the dead concerning identification, exact cause of death, manner of sustaining injuries and Clinical Forensic Medicine deals with the living in terms of examining and certifying injuries and weapons.

Apart from teaching Forensic Medicine and Toxicology to medical students, we also inculcate professional ethics and etiquettes to them thereby making them ethically competent in the modern era of Medical Practice.

Department has a state of the art mortuary with cold storage facilities to preserve and store bodies. Rare poisons, weapons, photographs and other specimens of forensic importance are all preserved and displayed in the Departmental Museum.

Services provided are -

  • Conducting post mortem examinations by the experts around the clock.

  • Equipped with facilities and manpower to conduct post mortems on the spot at the scene of crime.

  • Embalming and facilitating transport of dead bodies to distant places.

  • Examination of skeletal remains.

  • Providing expert opinion and deposing as expert witness in the Court of Law.

The Pharmacology Department at CDSIMER is a dynamic, multidisciplinary center of excellence dedicated to understanding drugs, their interactions with living systems, and other chemical substances capable of producing biological responses. Our mission is to provide high-quality medical education and foster cutting-edge research in areas such as:

Clinical Research and Development: Focused on the clinical development of pharmaceutical products, including advanced pharmacokinetic and therapeutic drug monitoring studies.

Pharmacovigilance and Safety: Operating an established Adverse Drug Reaction Monitoring Centre under the Pharmacovigilance Programme of India (PvPI).

Pharmacoeconomics and Rational Prescribing: Promoting evidence-based, cost-effective prescribing practices.

Preclinical Research and Toxicology: Performing translational research to bridge laboratory findings and clinical applications.

Materiovigilance and Device Safety: Monitoring and ensuring the safety of medical devices in collaboration with the Materiovigilance Programme of India (MvPI).

Professional Collaborations: Partnerships with leading bodies such as the Indian Pharmacological Society and the Medical Pharmacologists Society to organize training programs, national workshops, and seminars on research methodology, statistics, scientific writing, and communication skills.

Pharmacovigilance and Public Health Impact: Active involvement in pharmacovigilance through educational campaigns, short films, and a pioneering E-pharmacovigilance card to safeguard patients from adverse drug reactions.

Future Plans -

  1. State-of-the-Art Clinical Research Center: Fully equipped and statutorily approved by the Drugs Controller General of India (DCGI), NABH, and NABL. This center is open for industry-academia collaborations at both national and international levels with organizations like ICMR and WHO.

  2. Pharmacogenomics and Personalized Medicine: Conducting research at the molecular level to predict drug responses and develop safer, more effective treatment options.

  3. Innovative Projects and Patents: Contributing to global advancements in medicine through patented research, including hypokalemia prediction models and pharmacogenomics-based ADR detection.

  4. Innovative Teaching Modules: Utilizing AV/AI teaching tools and AR/VR clinical pharmacology techniques.

Vision for the Future -

Our department aims to be a global leader in pharmacological research and education. We are dedicated to innovation, collaboration, and a strong commitment to public health. Through these efforts, we strive to make meaningful contributions to scientific advancements and to the training of future healthcare professionals.

hotspot.description: Alexander Fleming (born August 6, 1881, Lochfield Farm, Darvel, Ayrshire, Scotland—died March 11, 1955, London, England) was a Scottish bacteriologist best known for his discovery of penicillin. Fleming had a genius for technical ingenuity and original observation. His work on wound infection and lysozyme, an antibacterial enzyme found in tears and saliva, guaranteed him a place in the history of bacteriology. But it was his discovery of penicillin in 1928, which started the antibiotic revolution, that sealed his lasting reputation. Fleming was recognized for that achievement in 1945, when he received the Nobel Prize for Physiology or Medicine, along with Australian pathologist Howard Walter Florey and German-born British biochemist Ernst Boris Chain, both of whom isolated and purified penicillin.

hotspot.description: Sir Henry Dale (born June 9, 1875, London, Eng.—died July 23, 1968, Cambridge) was an English physiologist who in 1936 shared the Nobel Prize for Physiology or Medicine with the German pharmacologist Otto Loewi for their discoveries in the chemical transmission of nerve impulses.After receiving his bachelor’s degree (1903) from the University of Cambridge, Dale began his research career in 1904 at the Wellcome Physiological Research Laboratories. In 1909 he completed his medical degree (M.D.) at Cambridge and in 1914 joined the staff of what later became the Medical Research Council. From 1928 to 1942 he was director of its subsidiary organization, the National Institute for Medical Research.

hotspot.description: Louis Pasteur (born December 27, 1822, Dole, France—died September 28, 1895, Saint-Cloud) was a French chemist and microbiologist who was one of the most important founders of medical microbiology. Pasteur’s contributions to science, technology, and medicine are nearly without precedent. He pioneered the study of molecular asymmetry; discovered that microorganisms cause fermentation and disease; originated the process of pasteurization; saved the beer, wine, and silk industries in France; and developed vaccines against anthrax and rabies.

He published Der grossen Wundartzney (Great Surgery Book) in 1536 and a clinical description of syphilis in 1530.

hotspot.description: Hippocrates (born c. 460 bce, island of Cos, Greece—died c. 375 bce, Larissa, Thessaly) was an ancient Greek physician who lived during Greece’s Classical period and is traditionally regarded as the father of medicine. It is difficult to isolate the facts of Hippocrates’ life from the later tales told about him or to assess his medicine accurately in the face of centuries of reverence for him as the ideal physician. About 60 medical writings have survived that bear his name, most of which were not written by him. He has been revered for his ethical standards in medical practice, mainly for the Hippocratic Oath, which, it is suspected, he did not write.

The “bench-to-bedside” approach takes advantage of laboratory research results in clinical settings, which can ultimately benefit patients. This translational research requires infrastructure to bridge the gap between basic sciences and medicine. The central research laboratory was established in 2022 on the fourth floor, G-block, Chandramma Dayananda Sagar Institute of Medical Education and Research (CDSIMER). The CRL is set up with the aim of encouraging integrated research projects across various departments and schools under Dayananda Sagar University. Also, we welcome collaborative research with other research institutions and universities across the globe. The CRL acts as a single-point facility for students and faculty researchers. Currently, the CRL is equipped to store biological samples and conduct various molecular biology experiments, including immunohistochemistry and genomic and therapeutic drug monitoring studies. Since its inception, we have completed an extramural grant project on therapeutic drug monitoring on anti-tubercular drugs and an intramural grant study on protein expression in human solid epithelial malignancies.


Two university-funded research projects on tuberculosis and type 2 diabetes patients are undergoing in the central research laboratory.

userdata.description:
Welcome to the Department of Respiratory Medicine at CDSIMER, Dayananda Sagar University—a beacon of excellence in pulmonary care, education, and research.

Situated amidst the tranquil setting of Harohalli, Ramanagara district, our department blends advanced medical practices with a compassionate, patient-centric approach. From managing Asthma, COPD to diagnosing lung cancer and sleep disorders, we provide comprehensive care for a wide range of respiratory conditions.

Our highly skilled team of faculty at the department, not only expertise in managing complex respiratory diseases but are also deeply invested in training the next generation of pulmonary specialists. Through hands-on learning and cutting-edge research, we equip students to tackle real-world challenges in respiratory health.

Recognizing the importance of community health, we actively partner with government and non-governmental agencies to address pressing issues like tuberculosis and occupational lung diseases. With molecular diagnostic tools like TrueNat and modern imaging facilities like CT scan & MRI, we ensure timely diagnosis and effective treatment for all.

Our outreach programs extend quality care to under-served areas. From respiratory health check-ups to smoking cessation support, we are committed to improving respiratory health at the grassroot level.

Our department leads the way in research and innovation, tackling challenges like emerging respiratory infections, Tuberculosis, asthma, and lung cancer. Collaborative projects and student involvement foster a culture of inquiry and discovery at a very early age.

With a vision to become a global center of excellence, we aim to set new benchmarks in pulmonary care, education, and research—ensuring a healthier, brighter future for all!

userdata.description:
The Department of Pediatrics is dedicated to providing comprehensive healthcare for children from birth through adolescence, integrating clinical excellence, education, and research. With state-of-the-art facilities such as the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) and Pediatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU), the department is equipped to manage a wide range of pediatric conditions with precisionand care.

Our outpatient services feature general pediatric clinics and specialized consultations in nutrition, neurology, cardiology, and high-risk newborn care. The department places a strong emphasis on dietary interventions, including tailored nutrition clinics and the implementation of Low-Carb High-Fat (LCHF) diets to combat metabolic syndrome in children and adolescents. Preventive care services such as immunization programs and adolescent counseling further underscore our holistic approach to pediatric health.

Inpatient care encompasses the management of infectious diseases, endocrine and neurological disorders, respiratory conditions, and complex cases requiring specialized attention. The Thalassemia Day Care Centre offers targeted transfusion therapies for affected children. For critical cases, the department provides round-the-clock emergency care, including neonatal resuscitation and advanced treatment for conditions like birth asphyxia, neonatal jaundice, meningitis, and diabetic ketoacidosis.

The department also actively engages in community outreach initiatives, including school health camps, diagnostic camps, and participation in national campaigns like Pulse Polio. Through a multidisciplinary approach, we integrate clinical expertise with compassionate care, focusing on fostering healthier futures for children. Our commitment to academic training and innovative research further drives advancements in pediatric healthcare, including nutritional strategies for addressing contemporary health challenges.
